editorNote: Two disclosures anchor today's edition: Alibaba's formal notice of a Hong Kong spin-off of its chip unit T-Head, and Rocket Lab's record third-quarter revenue alongside a wider loss and a Neutron debut now set for 2027 at the earliest. Other watchlist items could not be traced to a source we fetched, so the edition is short.

stories.headline: Alibaba says Hong Kong has cleared a spin-off listing of chip unit T-Head, with no timetable set
stories.summary: In a Nov. 10 filing, Alibaba said it will spin off T-Head through a Hong Kong listing of H shares, after the exchange confirmed it may proceed under Practice Note 15; T-Head confidentially filed its listing application on Sept. 11. Offering size and structure are not final, and the filing says there is no assurance the spin-off will happen or when.
stories.whyItMatters: The filing says T-Head would remain a subsidiary and that the spin-off is expected not to affect Alibaba's Hong Kong and NYSE listings; it still needs Listing Committee approval and a CSRC filing.

stories.headline: Rocket Lab posts record $267.8M Q3 revenue and a wider loss; Neutron first launch now no earlier than 2027
stories.summary: Rocket Lab reported Q3 2026 revenue of $267.8 million, up 73% from $155.1 million a year earlier, with a GAAP net loss of $79.7 million versus $18.3 million. Backlog rose to about $3.57 billion, up 52% from the end of Q2, and Q4 revenue guidance is $270 million to $290 million.
stories.whyItMatters: The release targets Neutron's first launch for no earlier than 2027, and the backlog includes 16 Neutron missions; adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $18.0 million from $26.3 million.

sourceLinks.title: Rocket Lab Q3 2026 results, Form 8-K exhibit 99.1 (SEC)
